US cash breadth, synchronized VXN/VIX, paired 10Y/2Y yields, primary FedWatch probabilities and contract-matched oil quotes remain unavailable.

editorial.marketOverview: The three-session Nasdaq/QQQ outlook remains bearish with elevated downside risk following Friday's technology and semiconductor liquidation. Monday's Reuters-timestamped 02:29 EST futures rebound (Nasdaq-100 +3.02%, S&P +2.24%) increases the credibility of a relief rally but cannot establish a US cash-market trend reversal. SOX's Friday weakness and divergent Asian chip-market response remain central.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters provides a 02:29 EST timestamp for the previously identified approximately 3% Nasdaq futures rebound. New Reuters coverage describes hedge-fund deleveraging after a greater-than-3% weekly loss and Taiwan's planned margin-maintenance reduction from 130% to 120% Tuesday. These reinforce existing rebound-versus-liquidation scenarios rather than a new bias. Curated Open Watch's Taiwan stabilization event was already incorporated.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Oversold conditions and regional policy support may produce sharp squeezes, but leveraged investor selling and extreme semiconductor underperformance constrain confidence. Distinguish Monday futures indications from confirmed US cash breadth, SOX participation, and volatility compression. Friday's 29bp indicative 10Y-2Y spread uses prior non-synchronized 4.94% and 4.65% inputs, not a live curve; all yields are in percent and spread in basis points.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: elevated chance of sharp opening relief, vulnerable to fade unless QQQ and SOX/SMH lead together and breadth improves. Tuesday November 24: assess persistence and consumer confidence/Dell earnings against Taiwan's scheduled collateral relief. Wednesday November 25: PCE/GDP and Beige Book create large rate and valuation sensitivity; downside risk persists if yields or volatility rise or semiconductors lag.
editorial.bullCase: A sustained US cash rally with SOX/SMH outperforming QQQ, expanding positive breadth, declining VXN/VIX and contained Treasury yields would validate the rebound and justify reassessing the bearish bias. Taiwan's stabilization steps may ease forced selling but are not themselves proof of a US recovery.
editorial.bearCase: A fading Nasdaq futures rally, renewed SOX weakness, deteriorating breadth, persistent volatility and higher oil/inflation expectations would confirm that the bounce is short-covering within a broader deleveraging phase. Reuters' hedge-fund exposure reduction adds structural fragility, though it is backward-looking.
editorial.watchNext: Watch the US cash open and first hour for QQQ/SOX/SMH leadership and breadth; obtain matched VXN/VIX and paired Treasury 10Y/2Y yields before drawing cross-market conclusions. Monitor Monday flash PMIs, Tuesday consumer confidence and Dell earnings, Wednesday PCE/GDP and Beige Book; verify FedWatch and same-contract Brent/WTI before assigning numerical probabilities or oil impacts.
